title: Redo role-prompt goal-preservation change and sweep 1,800 mentions
summary: Redo the rejected job from the base: edit the reader, producer and verifier prompts so a request's real goal survives to the verdict, make a non-empty request_reading_mismatch a Major finding in judge(), and raise the reader budget minimally. Sweep every 1,800 mention with a final Grep, and fix the verifier.md unclear "it"; doc line width is a nit only.

defaults_applied.how: Every 1,800 mention is swept, not only the ones that surfaced.
New judge() behavior has unit tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
decisions.md records the measured reader token count.
Single focused change limited to the prompts, judge(), budget and doc mentions.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: Athena's reader, producer and verifier agents, and the maintainer who judges whether a request's goal survived to the verdict.
Per the user's reply, doc line wrapping is a nit and not a criterion; the producer should still rewrap edited lines reasonably but nothing blocks on it.
The verifier.md 'it' referent nit is fixed in passing by naming Athena.
The self-check/introspection proposal is not part of this retry; the typed request is to redo the rejected job.
The file list follows the earlier accepted reading; I did not re-read the files.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md tells the reader to name the request's audience (who will use or judge the result) in the summary or assumptions.
reader.md requires at least one acceptance criterion written as an outcome the named audience can check; presence checks alone do not satisfy it.
reader.md forbids putting the request's own stated goal in out_of_scope, and tells the reader to read the current output the request is about before planning a change to it.
producer.md treats the acceptance criteria as a floor and tells the producer to serve the request's goal, while keeping the small-change and follow-conventions instructions.

verifier.md tells the verifier to judge user-facing output as its intended audience would, and to rate a request-reading mismatch at least major, never minor because the criteria passed. Sentences have clear referents (name Athena where Athena ran the commands).

In judge() in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, a non-empty request_reading_mismatch adds a Major finding and a reason, so the verdict is not pass. Unit tests cover mismatch present and absent or blank. Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify
The BudgetSet::Reader budget is raised only as far as the new reader text needs. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
docs/decisions.md records the new reader budget, the measured count and why removals cannot pay for the new rules; CHANGELOG.md notes the change.

A repo-wide Grep for 1,800 and 1800 finds no present-tense statement of the old reader budget: defaults-loop.md:47, :227, :413; decision-sets.md:107, :111; decisions.md:612; athena-v0.md:1507, :1868; socratic-review.md:176, :198 if present tense, :219 are updated. Past-tense review and history records may keep it, and dated review-1 measurements stay purely past figures.
The workspace stays clean and tested. Run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test

out_of_scope: Building the pre-verification self-check or changing rejection events (the introspection's proposal).
Changing past-tense review or history records that mention 1,800.
Enforcing doc line width by mechanism.
departures: Larger multi-file change with prompt, code, budget and many doc edits, plus a prior rejection history, so cost and time are above the reference.
